T-1: (T-1) WRAP's H-policy is a policy with the I^loc property, on every game. Define I(s) := the H-part of S4a′'s result at the standard state of s (§2.4-§2.7 hold at every standard state, reachable or not). It is a map on S_0(H); every v goes to a ⊴_s-best successor (the property); (1) holds (the new successor is not worse than the old); (2) holds (if some v has a strictly better successor it moves to a strictly better one). NT: (T-2) **Claim NT (no tie on a 1-sink game; mine).** Let G with ι be a 1-sink game in [F11] §5's sense, with sink x, and σ a player-0 strategy with Ξ_ι ⊴ Ξ_σ. Then Ξ_σ(u) ≠ Ξ_σ(u′) for all nodes u ≠ u′. Proof. By Sink Seeking (p. 8) every Ξ_σ(u) has cycle component x; every other node is more relevant than x (Sink Existence), so the cycle is x's loop and the path component of Ξ_σ(u) is the set of ALL nodes of the play from u before x, u itself included (the paper's own remark, p. 8: «the path-length component equals the cardinality of the path component»). Ξ_σ(x) = (x, ∅, 0) differs from every other value. If u, u′ ≠ x had equal values, u′ would lie on u's play and u on u′'s play; plays are positional, so u's play would return to u before reaching x: a cycle without x, against Sink Seeking. ∎
